name: Question 1
problem: Consider the vectors ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ and ${a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis of $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ by inspection.
worked_solution:
Remember that a basis of $S$ is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans $S.$

From the given vectors, we can see that ${a}_{2}$ is a linear combination of vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}:$

$$
{a}_{2}=2\cdot {a}_{1}+0\cdot {a}_{3}
$$

Consequently, the vector ${a}_{2}$ can be removed from $\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ without changing the span. So $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is spanned by just ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}}.$ 

Lastly, note that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}}$ is a linearly independent set that spans $S.$

Therefore, a basis of $S$ is ${{a}_{1},{a}_{3}},$ that is to say,

$$
B={{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{1}},{{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{a}_{3}}}.
$$

Question 1
?

Consider the vectors a1=[−10],a2=[−20], and a3=[−11]. Find a basis of S=Span{a1,a2,a3} by inspection.

a
B={[−10],[−20],[−11]}
b
B={[−10],[−11]}
c
B={[−11]}
d
B={[−10],[−20]}
e
B={[−20]}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Remember that a basis of S is a set of linearly independent vectors that spans S.

From the given vectors, we can see that a2 is a linear combination of vectors a1 and a3:

a2=2⋅a1+0⋅a3

Consequently, the vector a2 can be removed from Span{a1,a2,a3} without changing the span. So S=Span{a1,a2,a3} is spanned by just {a1,a3}.

Lastly, note that a1 and a3 are linearly independent since they are not parallel. So the set {a1,a3} is a linearly independent set that spans S.

Therefore, a basis of S is {a1,a3}, that is to say,

B={[−10]⏟a1,[−11]⏟a3}.
